chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abu al-Maghra' from Sama'ah from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard a man asking Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I was in his presence, about a son of a brother (nephew) and a grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth is to be divided between the two of them, in two halves.'
ai.seo_question: How is an estate divided between a nephew and a grandfather in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam (peace be upon him) establishes that a nephew (son of a brother) and a grandfather share the inheritance equally, each receiving half. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the grandfather, when present with a nephew, does not exclude him but rather stands as a co-heir, reflecting a distinct approach from some Sunni schools where the grandfather may exclude the nephew or share differently. The hadith underscores the principle of equitable distribution among close male relatives in the absence of closer heirs like sons or fathers.
